task.instructions:
Using matplotlib, plot the mean yield of five reaction conditions with explicit error bars showing the standard error of the mean.
  condition   mean yield (%)   SEM
  Baseline           42.1      2.3
  Cat-A              55.4      3.1
  Cat-B              61.8      1.9
  Cat-C              58.2      2.8
  Cat-D              49.7      4.2
Requirements:
1. Put the conditions on the x axis at positions 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 in the order listed, and use the condition names as the x tick labels.
2. Draw each mean as a marker (no connecting line is required) at its yield value.
3. Draw a symmetric vertical error bar of +/- one SEM on every point, and give the error bars visible end caps (pass capsize with a value greater than zero).
4. The y axis must start at 0 so the yields stay comparable.
5. Give the chart a title and label both axes.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Data
conditions = ['Baseline', 'Cat-A', 'Cat-B', 'Cat-C', 'Cat-D']
mean_yields = [42.1, 55.4, 61.8, 58.2, 49.7]
SEMs = [2.3, 3.1, 1.9, 2.8, 4.2]

# Positions for x-axis
positions = np.arange(len(conditions))

# Create plot
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
plt.errorbar(positions, mean_yields, yerr=SEMs, fmt='o', capsize=5, label='Mean Yield with SEM')

# Customize plot
plt.title('Mean Yield of Reaction Conditions with Standard Error of the Mean')
plt.xlabel('Reaction Conditions')
plt.ylabel('Mean Yield (%)')
plt.xticks(positions, conditions)
plt.ylim(0, max(mean_yields) + 5)  # Ensure y-axis starts at 0 and has some padding

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('figure.png')
plt.close()
